extracted.intended_audience: researchers and clinicians conducting or appraising interrater/intrarater reliability and psychometric validation studies (e.g., clinical researchers, biostatisticians, instrument developers)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, conducting, and reporting studies that estimate intra- and interrater agreement and reliability of clinical/measurement instruments using statistics such as kappa, ICC, percent agreement, and validity indices, and evaluating usability and applicability of appraisal tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intra- and interrater agreement and reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate intra- and interrater agreement and reliability with regard to describing/assessing clinical or imaging findings by having raters assess the same material (e.g., videoclips, images, examinations) possibly at different times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs include repeating assessments after a minimum interval (e.g., ≥2 months) to estimate intrarater reliability; raters should be blinded to their own and others' results. Report both agreement and reliability statistics because lack of reproducibility affects associations between features and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific agreement (per-category agreement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report specific agreement for individual outcome categories rather than only global measures; some categories (especially rare ones or many-category variables) may have poor specific agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that for binary variables, agreement may be better for absence than for presence; for variables with >2 categories, identify which categories show highest agreement (examples: not-defined midline, regular junction, three-layer pattern had best specific agreement in one study).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohen's kappa (κ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Cohen's kappa to quantify interrater reliability for categorical (typically binary or nominal) ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report kappa with interpretation (e.g., descriptors used in the literature: slight, fair, moderate, substantial, almost perfect). Provide confidence intervals and p-values where possible. Compare to a gold-standard diagnosis when applicable (e.g., telephone screening vs full exam).

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted kappa
rubrics_metrics.description: Use weighted kappa for ordinal categorical variables to account for degree of disagreement between categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report range of weighted kappa values for instrument items; useful when items have ordered categories (e.g., severity ratings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fleiss's kappa / multi-rater kappa
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Fleiss's multi-rater kappa (including free-marginal variants) to assess agreement across more than two raters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate for studies with multiple independent raters; report κ and interpret consistency across modalities (e.g., CTA vs DSA) and intra-rater repeats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ICC to assess reliability of continuous or interval measurements (examples: muscle thickness, cross-sectional area, aneurysm depth/length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify ICC model/type (e.g., ICC1.1, ICC3.1), report values with 95% CI. Interpret thresholds (one study notes ICC >0.75 as excellent). Distinguish intra- vs interrater ICCs and single-measure vs average-measure ICCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent agreement / concordance
rubrics_metrics.description: Report simple percent agreement or concordance on categorical measures alongside chance-corrected statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When categorical measures are dichotomized at logical points, use percent agreement and Cohen's Kappa for categorical measures; high concordance on overall scores can indicate strong item performance in generating reliable global assessment scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values
rubrics_metrics.description: For diagnostic screening tools, report sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV) against a gold-standard diagnosis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these metrics to evaluate telephone or remote screening tools compared to full clinical examination; report sample sizes and confidence intervals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cronbach's alpha (internal consistency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report Cronbach's alpha for internal consistency of scales or multi-item instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used alongside test-retest and interrater measures; report values and consider acceptable thresholds (e.g., alpha ~0.70+ often considered acceptable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gwet's AC1 statistic
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Gwet's AC1 as an alternative interrater reliability measure that is less sensitive to prevalence and marginal distributions than kappa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculate Gwet's AC1 for interrater reliability and also calculate weighted Cohen's kappa and Fleiss' kappa for comparability to previous evaluations; useful in tool-comparison studies (e.g., AMSTAR vs AMSTAR 2 vs ROBIS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Useability metrics: time to complete and time to consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure usability of appraisal tools by recording time to complete each assessment and time taken for reviewers to reach consensus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mean times to inform practical applicability and usability comparisons among tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity indices: content, construct, and criterion validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate and report content validity index, construct validity (e.g., factor analysis), and criterion validity when adapting or validating instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use forward/backward translation for cultural adaptation; report content validity index and factor structure (e.g., factors explaining variance) and plan further testing for criterion validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison to gold/reference standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare instrument or rater ratings to an established gold standard or phenomenological reference (e.g., full clinical exam, cluster-analysis defined reference groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report diagnostic accuracy (sensitivity, specificity, percent correctly classified) and inter-rater reliability (kappa) versus the reference standard; use reference-based evaluation to inform revisions of diagnostic criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical association and discrimination analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Use logistic regression, crosstabs, Spearman correlation, Fisher's exact test, chi-square tests to examine associations between instrument scores/levels and external variables or outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test associations between quality/risk assessments and study results/conclusions to inform applicability and interpretability of appraisal tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design/analysis procedural standards: sample selection, blinding, repeats
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ procedural controls such as selecting representative samples (e.g., consecutive patients), blinding raters to outcomes and to each other's ratings, and repeating a subset of scans for intra-rater reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify sample sizes, time intervals between repeats (e.g., ≥2 months), and number of raters; include repeated scans/recordings to estimate intra-rater agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dichotomization and categorical handling
rubrics_metrics.description: For analysis of categorical items, dichotomize responses at logical cut points for certain analyses and report kappa/concordance for those dichotomous comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about cut points and rationale; dichotomization may improve interpretability for some items but can lose information for multi-category variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of number of categories on reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that variables with many outcome categories can show poorer specific agreement and reliability than simpler/binary classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider using fewer categories or simplifying variables, or provide targeted rater training to improve agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rater training, standardization, and quality assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardize rater training and implement quality assurance programs to achieve and maintain high interrater reliability and diagnostic accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training can reduce differences between experienced and neophyte raters; standardization across study sites improves comparability of research findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective measurement standardization (device/procedure calibration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standardized measurement devices and protocols (e.g., apply a standardized 6 Nm force with a digital torque adapter) when quantifying physical measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardized devices can yield high rater-device agreement and improve reliability of quantified measures (report rater-device kappa/ICC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-source / multisource reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate reliability across multiple sources or rater types (e.g., parents vs clinicians, different professional raters) and consider combined/multi-source approaches for more comprehensive classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report interrater reliability between source types (e.g., parents vs SLTs) and recommend collaborative classification (professionals with parents) when it improves comprehensiveness.
